vendors.notes: IBM products (watsonx Orchestrate ADK, UI modernization, Carbon, Client Engineering building blocks) and the marketplace team's own accelerators. Packs are curated by the marketplace team from these official repositories with recorded provenance.

Curated from the public anthropics/skills repository. Only the Apache-2.0 skills are eligible; the document skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx) are source-available with a no-copy licence and stay out of the registry.
Curated from the Codex skills catalog (openai/skills). Each skill carries its own LICENSE.txt; only Apache-2.0 skills are taken.
Curated from google/skills (Apache-2.0): agent skills for Google Cloud, Gemini, Ads and Analytics.
Curated from hashicorp/agent-skills (MPL-2.0): Terraform and Packer skills.
Curated from microsoft/skills (MIT): Azure operations and SDK skills shipped as Claude Code plugins under .github/plugins/.

Curated from confluentinc/agent-skills (Apache-2.0): Kafka clients, Kafka Streams, Schema Registry, Flink and Confluent Cloud pipelines. Confluent has been an IBM company since March 2026 and keeps its own GitHub organisation, so it is listed as its own vendor, like HashiCorp.

packs.name: bob-essentials
packs.description: The marketplace inside Bob: find and install packs from chat, audit a skill before anyone trusts it, check the setup from hooks to MCP servers, and write new skills, modes, rules and commands. Ships /skills-add and a security rule that every task follows.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: The Bob Skills Marketplace inside Bob. Use when the user wants a skill or a capability Bob does not have installed, pastes a git link or a repository name and asks to install skills from it, asks what packs or skills exist ("is there a skill for X", "find a skill"), or asks to install, update, remove or explain a marketplace pack. Covers browsing the catalog offline, mapping a git link to a pack, showing what will be installed before confirming, accepting a vendor on first install, and refusing repositories outside the marketplace.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create or improve IBM Bob skills (SKILL.md plus optional scripts, references and assets), custom modes, rules and slash commands that Bob picks up and the marketplace policy linter accepts, with safe defaults built in - the user's yes before every external write, outside content treated as data, TLS on, loopback listeners, least-privilege modes. Use when the user wants to write a new skill, package a repeated workflow as a skill, fix a skill Bob ignores, create a custom mode, add a project rule or a slash command, or prepare any of them for a marketplace pack. Triggers include "create a skill", "write a SKILL.md", "package this as a skill", "the skill is not picked up", "create a mode", "add a rule", "make a slash command", "создай скилл", "создай режим".

skills.name: guard
skills.description: Explain and resolve a refusal from the uvx bob-skills guard hook, which checks every skill against .bob/skills.lock before Bob activates it. Use when a skill activation was refused with a "uvx bob-skills guard" message, or the user asks why a skill is blocked, mentions "unmanaged skill", "digest mismatch", "revoked version", "skill blocked", "guard", or wants to trust a local skill again.

skills.name: skill-audit
skills.description: Check a skill before anyone trusts or installs it - a skill copied from a repository, a web page or a colleague, the user's own skill, or an unmanaged skill the guard refused. Runs the marketplace policy linter, plus NVIDIA SkillSpector and Cisco skill-scanner when installed, then reads the skill for the holes scanners miss - writes or admin actions without the user's yes, instructions hidden in content the skill reads, TLS verification off, servers listening on all interfaces, stored credentials reused for unauthenticated requests. Use when the user asks "is this skill safe", "check this skill", "audit the skill", "can I trust it", "проверь скилл", or before `uvx bob-skills trust`.

skills.name: bob-doctor
skills.description: Check the Bob setup of this project and of ~/.bob and fix problems together with the user - guard hook missing, skills modified after install or unmanaged, skills Bob ignores, MCP servers with secrets in the config, unpinned versions, plain HTTP, TLS verification off, listeners on all interfaces, write tools approved in advance or telemetry on, and custom modes with unknown tool groups. Use when the user says "check my Bob setup", "doctor", "why is my skill or MCP server not working", "is my mcp.json safe", "проверь настройки Bob", or after installing packs or adding MCP servers by hand.

packs.name: ibm-cloud
packs.description: Find out what an IBM Cloud account holds, what it costs and why a VPC server, a cluster or a Code Engine app does not work. Read-only skills on the ibmcloud CLI; fixes come as commands you approve.

skills.name: ibmcloud-setup
skills.description: Check and prepare the IBM Cloud CLI before any IBM Cloud work - the CLI version, the plug-ins the ibm-cloud pack uses (VPC, Kubernetes Service, Code Engine), whether a session is open and which account, region and resource group it targets, and whether API tracing is on. Guides federated (SSO) login, where the user types the one-time passcode in their own terminal, and login with an API key from the environment. Use it first in any IBM Cloud task and whenever a command fails with "Not logged in", a missing plug-in or the wrong account. Triggers include "check my IBM Cloud setup", "log in to IBM Cloud", "which IBM Cloud account am I on", "ibmcloud says not logged in", "настрой ibmcloud", "в каком я аккаунте IBM Cloud".

skills.name: ibmcloud-inventory
skills.description: Inventory an IBM Cloud account, read-only - every resource instance with its service, resource group, region, state and tags, exported to CSV and JSON, with the findings worth a look - untagged instances, instances that are not active, instances left in the default resource group, and groups the session cannot see. Use when the user asks what they have in IBM Cloud, wants a list or spreadsheet of their resources, a tagging or clean-up review, or a picture of the landscape by service and group. Triggers include "what is in my IBM Cloud account", "list my IBM Cloud resources", "IBM Cloud inventory", "find untagged resources", "что у меня в IBM Cloud", "список ресурсов в облаке", "инвентаризация IBM Cloud".

skills.name: ibmcloud-diagnose
skills.description: Diagnose why something in IBM Cloud does not work, read-only. A VPC virtual server that cannot be reached or cannot reach out (instance state, floating IP and public gateway, security groups, stateless network ACLs in both directions); an IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service or Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud cluster that is unhealthy (master, Ingress, workers, versions, zones); a Code Engine application that is not ready or whose newest revision failed (reasons, events, known failure patterns, log tail); and "not authorized" errors from the CLI. Every fix is shown as a command and runs only after the user says yes. Use when the user reports a timeout to a VSI, a closed port, a cluster in warning, a worker not ready, a failed Code Engine deployment or a 403. Triggers include "can't connect to my VSI", "port 443 not reachable", "cluster is in warning", "Code Engine app failed", "revision not ready", "не открывается сервер в VPC", "кластер в warning", "приложение Code Engine не стартует".

skills.name: ibmcloud-cost
skills.description: Show where the IBM Cloud money goes, read-only - cost per service, per resource group and per instance for a month, the change against the previous month, the top spenders, and instances billed while their usage is zero, from the IBM Cloud usage reports. Works with the role the user has - account billing access gives the whole account, a resource group administrator gets that group - and names the role needed for anything the role does not allow. Never stops, scales or deletes anything. Use for "how much do we spend on IBM Cloud", "why did the bill go up", "what costs the most", "cost by resource group", "cloud cost report", "сколько мы тратим в IBM Cloud", "почему вырос счёт", "расходы по группам ресурсов".

safety.warning: The skills run the ibmcloud CLI in the session you opened, which carries every right your account gives you. A command outside the pack's read-only set could change or delete resources.
safety.covered: The pack's scripts only list and read. The `ibm-cloud` rule makes every changing command wait for your yes to that exact command, and `cloud-ops` mode writes only under `ibmcloud-reports/`. For the strictest setup, log in with an access group or service ID that has Viewer roles only.

safety.warning: Resource names, tags, event messages and application logs come from the account and can carry text aimed at the agent.
safety.covered: The rule and every skill treat them as data: they are quoted to you, never followed.

packs.name: ibm-watsonx-data-integration
packs.description: Build, run, diagnose and operate data flows in IBM watsonx.data integration (DataStage, pyflow) from natural language: flow lifecycle, DataStage and pyflow authoring, failed-run investigation, engine knowledge and bug reports. IBM's official skills, used with the Agentic Data Integration MCP server on IBM Cloud.

skills.name: di-agent-flow-lifecycle
skills.description: Entry point for ALL flow work in watsonx.data integration — creating, editing, running, diagnosing a failed run, or backing up/restoring a flow. Load this FIRST whenever a request touches a data flow. It gathers intent — including which engine the flow runs on — routes to exactly one lifecycle state, and applies a fixed precedence order so routing is consistent run to run.

skills.name: di-agent-flow-datastage
skills.description: Reference for the verbose watsonx.data integration SDK for DataStage (batch) flows, with exhaustive stage and property access — the full engine stage catalog. Load this only after the di-agent-flow-lifecycle router has selected the datastage-sdk authoring backend — this is a syntax and stage reference, not a decision about whether to use it. If you have not routed yet, load di-agent-flow-lifecycle instead.

skills.name: di-agent-flow-pyflow
skills.description: API spec for pyflow, IBM's LLM-optimized Python DSL for authoring DataStage and StreamSets flows. Its compact surface and compile-time validation offer context efficiency, fast feedback, and correctness guarantees. Load this only after the di-agent-flow-lifecycle router has selected the pyflow authoring backend — this is a language reference, not a decision about whether to use it. If you have not routed yet, load di-agent-flow-lifecycle instead.

skills.name: di-agent-datastage-investigation
skills.description: Deep investigation of a failed run of a DataStage job already in operation — a scheduled or production job, or any job whose failure the user asks you to investigate. Works end-to-end from MCP tools: logs, job config, flow structure, connection health. Produces a root-cause diagnosis, not a fix. NOT for a run that failed while a flow was being built or edited — those are handled by the di-agent-flow-lifecycle skill, which runs its own investigation and loads this one only when a production-depth analysis is needed.

skills.name: di-agent-knowledge-engine-datastage
skills.description: Q&A reference for the DataStage parallel engine — parallelism, partitioning theory, APT configuration files, concurrent job execution, restart/recovery, disk/resource tuning, dataset performance, flow optimization (partitioning/sorting/memory), and per-stage semantics. Use for conceptual engine questions and stage property lookups regardless of authoring tool.

skills.name: di-agent-bug-report
skills.description: Generates a Markdown bug report for an IBM watsonx.data integration session. User can invoke directly. The agent MUST propose it (and must wait for explicit acceptance) after 3 or more consecutive calls to the same tool or the same sequence of tools result in a failure or the same error. Skip for non-watsonx.data integration sessions.

safety.warning: The flow skills run, re-run, restore and delete jobs and assets in your watsonx.data integration instance, and a run whose write mode is `overwrite` truncates the target table.
safety.covered: This pack's rule requires your yes for each run, retry, restore and delete, names the target connections and the write mode first, and treats job logs and data rows as data.

packs.name: office-docs
packs.description: Create, edit, fill and extract Word documents, PowerPoint decks and Excel workbooks from Bob with python-docx, python-pptx and openpyxl. Original IBM skills with tested helper scripts; nothing leaves the machine.

skills.name: docx
skills.description: Create, edit, fill and extract Microsoft Word (.docx) files with python-docx through four ready-made scripts. Build a document from a JSON spec of headings, paragraphs, bullet and numbered lists, tables, images and page breaks (optionally on top of a template that keeps its styles, headers and footers), replace {{placeholders}} in a template even when Word split them across runs, dump the headings, text and tables of a .docx to Markdown or JSON, and convert to PDF with LibreOffice. Use it whenever a user asks to "create a Word document", "write a .docx report", "fill this Word template", "extract the text from this docx", "add a table to the document", "convert the docx to PDF" or "edit the Word file", or names a .docx file as input or output. Do not use for PDF, spreadsheet or presentation files unless a .docx is the input or the output.

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Create, edit, fill, extract and render PowerPoint (.pptx) decks with python-pptx and tested helper scripts. Builds a 16:9 deck from a Markdown outline (title slide, nested bullets, images, native bar/line/pie charts, speaker notes, optional corporate .pptx or .potx template), finds and replaces text across slides and notes while keeping run formatting, dumps an existing deck to Markdown with slide numbers, and renders it to PDF and PNG with LibreOffice for review. Use it when the user says "create a PowerPoint", "make a slide deck", "build slides from this outline", "add a chart to the presentation", "update the text in this pptx", asks about "speaker notes", wants to "export the deck to PDF", or names a .pptx file or a .potx template. Not for PDF, Word or Excel files unless a slide deck is the input or output.

skills.name: xlsx
skills.description: Create, edit, analyse or analyze Excel workbooks (.xlsx/.xlsm) and convert CSV or TSV files with openpyxl. Builds sheets from a JSON spec with a styled frozen header, number formats (currency, percent, date), live formulas, a totals row, autofilter, native bar/line/pie charts and dropdown validation; converts CSV/TSV exports into typed sheets; reports what an existing workbook contains (sheets, header, formulas, charts, names, merged cells); and checks formulas for errors through a LibreOffice recalculation or a static scan. Use it whenever the input or the deliverable is a spreadsheet file, for requests such as "create an Excel file", "build a spreadsheet", "add formulas to the workbook", "convert this CSV to xlsx", "what is in this Excel file", "add a chart to the sheet" or "fix the broken formulas"; not for Word, PowerPoint or PDF files.

skills.name: pdf
skills.description: Read, create, fill and manipulate PDF files with five ready-made scripts built on pypdf, pdfplumber and reportlab. Extract text per page (page ranges, layout mode, scanned-PDF detection), pull tables out as Markdown or CSV, build a report PDF from a JSON spec (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images, page numbers, Unicode font so Hebrew, Arabic and Cyrillic render), merge, split, rotate, watermark, compress, encrypt and set metadata, list and fill AcroForm fields, and OCR scanned pages locally with tesseract and poppler. Use it whenever a user says "extract the text from this PDF", "pull the tables out of the PDF", "merge these PDFs", "split the PDF into pages", "create a PDF report", "fill in this PDF form", "the PDF is scanned, OCR it" or "add a watermark to the PDF", or names a .pdf file as input or output. Not for Word, Excel or PowerPoint files unless a PDF is involved.

packs.name: presentations
packs.description: From a topic or your own data to a deck and the talk around it: one headline per slide, a style picked from five, charts and pictures. The same storyboard builds an interactive HTML deck, a printable PDF and a 16:9 PowerPoint.

skills.name: presentation
skills.description: Make a presentation from scratch or from the user's material (data, documents, notes) as one workflow. A brief, a story with one headline per slide, five conceptually different style concepts previewed as an HTML page for the user to choose from, charts and pictures, then the deck itself, by default as an interactive HTML presentation to click through or share as a link, and on request as a PDF or a styled 16:9 PowerPoint file from the same storyboard. Ends with a talk kit (pitch versions, speaker notes, Q&A bank, one-pager, follow-up email). Use when the user asks for a presentation, a deck, slides, a pitch deck, a keynote, a board or investor update, a conference talk, a training deck, or says "сделай презентацию", "подготовь слайды", "нужна дека", "презентация по этим данным". The step skills deck-story, deck-style, deck-dataviz, deck-images and deck-pitch cover single steps; this skill runs them in order.

skills.name: deck-story
skills.description: Build the story of a presentation. Choose a narrative structure, write one headline per slide, and check that the headlines alone tell the story. Works from scratch (an interview of eight questions), from the user's data (six lenses that turn a spreadsheet into three to five findings) or from a document. Use when the user asks how to structure a talk or a deck, says the deck has no story or "too many slides", wants an outline or a storyboard before slides exist, asks what to put on which slide, or says "структура презентации", "как рассказать эту историю", "сделай сторилайн". The presentation skill calls this as its story step.

skills.name: deck-style

Generates an HTML preview page with five conceptually different style concepts drawn on the deck's own five slides by the same renderer that builds the deck, so the preview is the deck, and turns the user's answer into a theme.json that the PowerPoint builder, the HTML deck, the chart renderer and the image scripts all read. Fifteen built-in concepts from minimal Swiss and IBM Carbon to a cyber steel HUD, pencil sketch, geometric poster and a dark midnight gold; each with its own ornament, every set of five keeps a dark option, contrast checked, brand colour and Cyrillic, Hebrew or Arabic fonts supported. Use when the user asks how the deck should look, wants to see options or a mockup before slides are built, mentions colours, fonts, corporate branding or a template, or says "выбери стиль", "покажи варианты оформления", "не нравится дизайн".

skills.name: deck-dataviz
skills.description: Make the charts of a presentation say one thing and look like part of the deck. Chooses the chart from the message rather than the data shape, writes native PowerPoint chart blocks for bar, line, area and pie, and renders waterfall, slope, lollipop, bullet, small multiples, scatter and heatmap charts to PNG in the deck's theme colours with matplotlib, offline. Use when a slide needs a chart or a graph, when a chart is unreadable or cluttered, when the user asks which chart to use, how to visualise numbers, wants to highlight one bar or add a target line, or says "как показать эти данные", "сделай график", "перерисуй диаграмму".

skills.name: deck-images
skills.description: Pictures for a presentation. Bundled Carbon icons and pattern tiles, generated backdrops, prompts for images the user makes once and reuses, plus where to get photographs legally and how to place everything so the deck looks designed. Covers open image sets (public domain, Creative Commons, Unsplash and similar, icon and illustration sets) with their licences and the credits record, prompts for image generators that match the deck's theme, and offline scripts that make on-theme abstract backdrops in SVG or PNG for title and section slides, apply one consistent treatment to the user's photos (crop, duotone, tint, scrim) and produce labelled placeholders for pictures that have not arrived yet. Use when a deck needs photos, illustrations, icons or a background, when the user asks where to find images, whether an image may be used, how to generate one, or says "нужны картинки", "найди изображения", "сгенерируй фон".

skills.name: deck-pitch
skills.description: Everything around the slides. The spoken pitch at four lengths, a per-slide talk track with timings, a Q&A bank with prepared answers and backup slides, a one-page leave-behind, the follow-up email, a rehearsal plan and a day-of checklist. Written from the deck's own storyboard so every answer points at a slide. Use when the user has a deck and needs to present it, asks how to open or close, what to say per slide, how long it will take, what questions to expect, how to handle a hostile question, wants an elevator pitch or a one-pager, or says "подготовь питч", "какие вопросы зададут", "что говорить на слайдах".

packs.name: google-cloud-data
packs.description: Work with BigQuery from an agent: basics, BigFrames data science, AI and ML in BigQuery, plus gcloud CLI guidance. Curated from Google's official agent skills.

skills.name: bigquery-basics
skills.description: Manages datasets, tables, and jobs in BigQuery. Use when you need to interact with BigQuery, run SQL queries, manage BigQuery resources (datasets, tables, views), or perform basic data ingestion and analysis.

skills.name: bigquery-bigframes
skills.description: Generates Python code using BigQuery DataFrames (BigFrames), the pandas/scikit-learn-style API over BigQuery. Use when writing BigFrames code or doing pandas-style dataframe/ML work against BigQuery (e.g. in a notebook). Don't use for SQL-first workflows or the google-cloud-bigquery client library — use bigquery-basics.

skills.name: bigquery-ai-ml
skills.description: Leverages BigQuery's built-in machine learning and GenAI capabilities for advanced data analytics. Use when you need to write SQL queries that perform time-series forecasting, predict values, detect outliers or anomalies, find key drivers, perform semantic search or vector search, classify text, calculate similarity, summarize content, translate language, evaluate models, filter by semantic conditions, or leverage generative AI capabilities in BigQuery. Do not use for general BigQuery dataset, table, or job management requests.

skills.name: gcloud
skills.description: Provides safety-critical validation, guardrails, and data reduction for gcloud CLI operations across Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services and infrastructure. Use when planning, generating, constructing, proposing, describing, or executing any gcloud CLI commands - including when answering questions about gcloud syntax, or formatting flags. Don't use when writing Google Cloud client library code or raw REST/gRPC API requests.

safety.warning: The BigQuery skills run DDL and DML, delete datasets and tables with `bq rm -f`, train models and call billable AI functions over whole tables, and the vendor text does not stop to ask first.
safety.covered: The security-defaults rule from bob-essentials makes the agent show each write, delete or billable query with its target and wait for your yes; ask for a LIMITed sample before an AI function runs over a table.

packs.name: hashicorp-terraform
packs.description: Terraform the way HashiCorp writes it: style guide, tests, policy as code, module refactoring, and importing existing infrastructure with search. Curated from hashicorp/agent-skills.

skills.name: terraform-style-guide
skills.description: Generate Terraform HCL code following HashiCorp's official style conventions and best practices. Use when writing, reviewing, or generating Terraform configurations.

skills.name: terraform-test
skills.description: Comprehensive guide for writing and running Terraform tests. Use when creating test files (.tftest.hcl), writing test scenarios with run blocks, validating infrastructure behavior with assertions, mocking providers and data sources, testing module outputs and resource configurations, or troubleshooting Terraform test syntax and execution.

skills.name: terraform-policy
skills.description: Write, test, or convert Terraform Policy files (.policy.hcl, .policytest.hcl, Sentinel→tfpolicy). Triggers: policy.hcl, policytest, convert sentinel, tfpolicy, write a policy.

skills.name: refactor-module
skills.description: Transform monolithic Terraform configurations into reusable, maintainable modules following HashiCorp's module design principles and community best practices.

skills.name: terraform-search-import
skills.description: Discover existing cloud resources using Terraform Search queries and bulk import them into Terraform management. Use when bringing unmanaged infrastructure under Terraform control, auditing cloud resources, or migrating to IaC.

safety.warning: terraform-test creates real infrastructure by default, and the import and refactor skills run `terraform apply` and `terraform state mv` on live state.
safety.covered: The security-defaults rule requires your yes for each apply or state move; run tests with `command = plan` or mocks first, and check that the plan shows no destroys before you approve it.

packs.name: microsoft-azure-ops
packs.description: Day-to-day Azure work from an agent: look up resources, manage storage, analyse cost, check compliance and quotas, diagnose failing resources and run compute. Curated from Microsoft's official skills repository.

skills.name: azure-resource-lookup
skills.description: List, find, and show Azure resources across subscriptions or resource groups. Handles prompts like "list the websites in my subscription", "list my web apps", "show my app services", "list virtual machines", "list my VMs", "show storage accounts", "find container apps", and "what resources do I have". USE FOR: list websites, list web apps, list app services, show websites in subscription, resource inventory, find resources by tag, tag analysis, orphaned resource discovery (not for cost analysis), unattached disks, count resources by type, cross-subscription lookup, and Azure Resource Graph queries. DO NOT USE FOR: deploying/changing resources (use azure-deploy), cost optimization (use azure-cost), or non-Azure clouds.

skills.name: azure-storage
skills.description: Azure Storage Services including Blob Storage, File Shares, Queue Storage, Table Storage, and Data Lake. Answers questions about storage access tiers (hot, cool, cold, archive), when to use each tier, and tier comparison. Provides object storage, SMB file shares, async messaging, NoSQL key-value, and big data analytics. Includes lifecycle management. USE FOR: blob storage, file shares, queue storage, table storage, data lake, upload files, download blobs, storage accounts, access tiers, storage tiers, hot cool cold archive, storage tier comparison, when to use storage tiers, lifecycle management, Azure Storage concepts. DO NOT USE FOR: SQL databases, Cosmos DB (use azure-prepare), messaging with Event Hubs or Service Bus (use azure-messaging).

skills.name: azure-cost
skills.description: Azure cost management: query costs, forecast spending, optimize to reduce waste. WHEN: "Azure costs", "Azure bill", "cost breakdown", "how much am I spending", "forecast spending", "optimize costs", "reduce spending", "orphaned resources", "rightsize VMs", "cost spike", "reduce storage costs", "AKS cost". DO NOT USE FOR: deploying resources, provisioning, diagnostics, or security audits.

skills.name: azure-compliance
skills.description: Run Azure compliance and security audits with azqr plus Key Vault expiration checks. Covers best-practice assessment, resource review, policy/compliance validation, and security posture checks. WHEN: compliance scan, security audit, BEFORE running azqr (compliance cli tool), Azure best practices, Key Vault expiration check, expired certificates, expiring secrets, orphaned resources, compliance assessment.

skills.name: azure-quotas
skills.description: Check/manage Azure quotas and usage across providers. For deployment planning, capacity validation, region selection. WHEN: "check quotas", "service limits", "current usage", "request quota increase", "quota exceeded", "validate capacity", "regional availability", "provisioning limits", "vCPU limit", "how many vCPUs available in my subscription".

skills.name: azure-diagnostics
skills.description: Debug Azure production issues on Azure using AppLens, Azure Monitor, resource health, and safe triage. WHEN: debug production issues, troubleshoot app service, app service high CPU, app service deployment failure, troubleshoot container apps, troubleshoot functions, troubleshoot AKS, VM RDP, Linux SSH, VM black screen, can't connect to VM, reset VM password, NSG or firewall blocking, kubectl cannot connect, kube-system/CoreDNS failures, pod pending, crashloop, node not ready, upgrade failures, analyze logs, KQL, insights, image pull failures, cold start issues, health probe failures, resource health, root cause of errors, troubleshoot event hubs, troubleshoot service bus, messaging SDK error, AMQP connection failure, message lock lost, service bus dead letter.

skills.name: azure-compute
skills.description: Azure VM/VMSS router. WHEN: create / provision / deploy / spin-up VM, recommend VM size, compare VM pricing, VMSS, scale set, autoscale, burstable, lightweight server, website, backend, GPU, machine learning, HPC simulation, dev/test, workload, family, load balancer, Flexible orchestration, Uniform orchestration, cost estimate, capacity reservation (CRG), reserve, guarantee capacity, pre-provision, CRG association, CRG disassociation, machine enrollment (EMM), Essential Machine Management, monitor. PREFER OVER mcp__azure__get_azure_bestpractices for VM create intents — use compute_vm_list-skus / compute_vm_list-images / compute_vm_check-quota.

safety.warning: The diagnostics and compute skills run commands inside virtual machines, reset passwords, exec into AKS pods and start privileged debug pods, and they apply fixes such as scaling a plan up.
safety.covered: The security-defaults rule makes the agent show each command and its target and wait for your yes; ask for read-only checks and `--dry-run` first, and delete debug pods when the investigation ends.

safety.warning: Capacity reservations bill from the moment they exist, whether or not a virtual machine uses them, and several workflows create or enable billable resources.
safety.covered: The rule requires the monthly cost and the exact resource to be shown before creation, and your yes for that action.

packs.name: microsoft-foundry
packs.description: Build and operate agents and models on Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry): projects, deployments, evaluation, tracing and the Foundry SDKs. Microsoft's most installed agent skill, curated from the official repository.

skills.name: microsoft-foundry
skills.description: Build, deploy, evaluate, optimize, fine-tune, and manage Microsoft Foundry agents, models, and resources end to end. USE FOR: azd ai agent, azd provision/deploy, hosted agent scaffold/develop/run/deploy/troubleshoot, prompt agent create, create agent, update agent, add tool to agent, invoke agent, agent.yaml, evaluate agent, batch eval, continuous eval, continuous monitoring, agent CI/CD, optimize prompt, improve prompt, prompt optimizer, optimize agent instructions, Agent Optimizer scaffold, dataset curation from traces, deploy model, model fine-tuning (SFT/DPO/RFT), Foundry project, RBAC, role assignment, permissions, quota, capacity, region, deployment failure, AI Services, create Foundry resource, knowledge index, customize deployment, onboard, availability, training-data, grader, distillation, large file upload. DO NOT USE FOR: Azure Functions, App Service, general Azure deploy (use azure-deploy), general Azure prep (use azure-prepare).

safety.warning: The workflows deploy models, delete deployments and files, submit fine-tuning jobs and assign RBAC roles, and several steps tell the agent to go ahead on its own.
safety.covered: The security-defaults rule overrides those steps: each deploy, delete, role assignment or billable job needs your yes, with the SKU, capacity and cost shown first.

safety.warning: Some steps collect secrets through the chat and write them into environment files, and the local-run examples listen on every network interface.
safety.covered: The rule keeps secrets in your environment or Key Vault and out of chat and project files, and keeps local servers on 127.0.0.1.

packs.name: confluent-kafka
packs.description: Build Kafka producers, consumers and Kafka Streams apps with Schema Registry, bring unmanaged schemas under Schema Registry with PII tags, write Flink SQL and Java UDFs, set up CDC pipelines into Iceberg or Delta tables with Tableflow, and plan a move from AWS MSK to Confluent Cloud. Confluent's official skills, curated from confluentinc/agent-skills with the evals Confluent scores them against.

skills.name: developing-kafka-java-client
skills.description: Use when the user wants to integrate a Kafka client into an existing application or scaffold a Java Kafka client project (Maven or Gradle based) for Confluent Cloud, local Docker, or WarpStream. Covers the Apache Kafka Java clients (KafkaProducer/KafkaConsumer/KafkaShareConsumer) with Avro, JSON Schema, or Protobuf serializers. Also use when the user wants to optimize Java Kafka client configuration for WarpStream. Do NOT trigger for Kafka Streams apps (use kafka-streams-programming), Flink, connectors, or Kafka Python client (use developing-kafka-python-client).

skills.name: developing-kafka-python-client
skills.description: Use when the user wants to build a Python Kafka producer or consumer, add Schema Registry to existing Python code, migrate from raw JSON to schema-backed serialization, or scaffold a confluent-kafka-python project for Confluent Cloud, local Docker, or WarpStream. Also use when user wants to optimize Python Kafka client configuration for WarpStream.

skills.name: kafka-streams-programming
skills.description: Architect, build, and debug Kafka Streams apps (JVM-embedded stream processing). Use when user mentions KStream, KTable, topology, TopologyTestDriver, StreamsBuilder, interactive queries, GlobalKTable, joins/windows/aggregations, or debugging issues (rebalancing, state stores, lag, deserialization errors). Also use when user wants to optimize Kafka Streams for WarpStream or tune Kafka Streams client configuration for WarpStream. Do NOT trigger for Flink, connectors, CDC, or plain producer/consumer.

skills.name: kafka-schema-registry
skills.description: Scan a project to identify Kafka applications, extract schemas from data models, tag PII fields, generate Terraform for Confluent Schema Registry registration, and produce a migration report with rollout ordering. Use this skill when a user asks to analyze a folder or repo for Kafka usage, extract schemas, audit producer/consumer configurations, or generate Terraform for Schema Registry.

skills.name: flink-udf
skills.description: Build and deploy Apache Flink user-defined functions (UDFs) in Java for stream processing over Kafka. Use this skill when users want to create scalar UDFs, user-defined table functions (UDTFs), or process table functions (PTFs) in Java, deploy them to Confluent Cloud or local Docker environments, and invoke them from Flink SQL or the Table API. Trigger on: Flink UDF, custom Flink function, process table function, PTF, UDTF, Flink user defined, extend Flink SQL, stateful stream processing with Flink. Do NOT trigger for: Kafka Streams UDFs (use kafka-streams-programming skill), general Flink job development without custom functions, CDC streaming data piplines that include Flink (prefer the confluent-cloud-cdc-tableflow skill), Flink connector setup, or Kafka producer/consumer code.

skills.name: confluent-cloud-flink-sql
skills.description: Write and debug Flink SQL that runs on Confluent Cloud, enforcing the CC-vs-Apache-Flink (OSS) dialect boundary. Use when the working directory is a Confluent Cloud Flink workspace, when a Flink SQL statement needs checking before it runs on a CC compute pool, or when the user mentions CC Flink, Confluent Cloud Flink SQL, the `confluent flink` CLI, a CFU compute pool, `CREATE CONNECTION`, or asks to check or debug Flink SQL whose runtime is Confluent Cloud. Also trigger when a Flink SQL question is posed and nothing establishes an Apache Flink OSS runtime. Do NOT trigger for: building or deploying Flink UDFs in Java (UDF/UDTF/PTF — use flink-udf); a full CDC pipeline from a database through Flink into Tableflow/Iceberg/Delta Lake (use confluent-cloud-cdc-tableflow); Kafka Streams topology work (use kafka-streams-programming); or Flink SQL confirmed to run on Apache Flink OSS, not Confluent Cloud.

skills.name: confluent-cloud-cdc-tableflow
skills.description: Set up end-to-end Change Data Capture (CDC) pipelines on Confluent Cloud using Debezium source connectors, Flink for transformation, and Tableflow for data lake integration. Supports JSON_SR, Avro, and Protobuf formats. Handles schemaless topics (plain JSON without SR) and multi-event topics. This skill handles the complete workflow from database to Iceberg/Delta tables. Use this skill when users want to capture database changes and materialize them into Iceberg or Delta Lake tables via Confluent Cloud Tableflow. Trigger phrases include "CDC to Tableflow", "database to Iceberg", "database to Delta Lake", "stream database changes to data lake", "set up Tableflow pipeline", "schemaless topic to Tableflow", or "multi-event topic to Iceberg". Do NOT trigger for general CDC, Debezium, or database replication requests that do not involve Tableflow or Iceberg/Delta Lake as the destination.

skills.name: msk-migration
skills.description: Use this skill to assess and plan a migration from AWS MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) to Confluent Cloud. Triggers on user intent like "migrate MSK to Confluent Cloud", "move off MSK", "MSK to CC cutover", "Zero-Cut migration from MSK", "kcp scan my MSK", or any discussion of MSK-to-CC assessment, planning, cluster sizing, Cluster Linking setup, Gateway-based switchover, or post-cutover validation. Do NOT trigger for non-MSK Kafka sources (open-source Kafka, Aiven, Confluent Platform, Redpanda) — this skill is MSK-only. Do NOT trigger for greenfield Confluent Cloud projects with no existing Kafka source. Do NOT trigger for general Kafka programming questions (producer/consumer code, Kafka Streams) unrelated to migration.

safety.warning: The Confluent Cloud skills create and delete environments, connectors, topics and Flink statements, and Flink statements consume CFUs while they run.
safety.covered: The skills present a plan and run EXPLAIN before CREATE; the security-defaults rule adds a yes per create or delete, named by object and environment. The teardown script asks once before it deletes the demo topics and local state.

safety.warning: The bundled docker-compose files publish the broker, REST proxy and Schema Registry without authentication on every network interface, and the setup guides write cluster keys into local properties files.
safety.covered: Publish those ports as `127.0.0.1:PORT:PORT` when you run them, and add the key files to `.gitignore` as the Java skill does.
